Heredoc bodies and sub-less special subs, written back as the source wrote
them (issue 01a16602-5fd5). perl reads a heredoc's body from the line after
its opener's and then resumes the statement, so canon writes a body inside a
statement's span where the source put it: after the code that ended the
opener's line, ahead of the next node, or ahead of the closers and `;` that
follow it. A sub-less `DESTROY { ... }` or `AUTOLOAD { ... }` is the sub
perl's yyl_sub reads at a statement boundary, and canon writes it without
`sub`. Neither is forgiven by Faithful. Each Deparse,-p is perl 5.44.0's.

=== two heredocs in an argument list that runs on (op/debug.t)
fresh_perl_is(<<'CODE', <<'EXPECT',
use B qw(SVf_IOK);
CODE
Done
EXPECT
    {}, 'debugger');
--- facts
anonhash 1 exact
faithful
# fresh_perl_is("use B qw(SVf_IOK);\n", "Done\n", scalar({}), 'debugger');

=== a heredoc after a string in a multi-line list (op/hook/require.t)
fresh_perl_is(
    'require Apack;',
    <<'EOF_WANT',
before Apack.pm at - line 1.
EOF_WANT
    { },
    'post action');
--- facts
anonhash 1 exact
faithful

=== a heredoc whose line ends after the next argument (op/attrs.t)
fresh_perl_is('our $d : Dummy', <<EOS, {},
Invalid SCALAR attribute.
EOS
    "same name");
--- facts
anonhash 1 exact
faithful

=== a body before the statement's semicolon (op/hash-rt85026.t)
print <<"EOF"
body
EOF
;
--- facts
faithful
# print("body\n");

=== a body before the call's closing paren (op/threads.t)
fresh_perl_is(
 <<'   EOJ', 'ok'
   use threads;
   EOJ
);
--- facts
faithful

=== a body as a block's last statement, with no semicolon (op/magic.t)
my ($x, $m);
if ($x) {
  $m = <<'EOX'
body
EOX
}
--- facts
faithful
# if ($x) { ($m = "body\n"); }

=== a body before a sub's first statement
f(1, <<"E", sub {
body
E
  2; });
--- facts
faithful
# f(1, "body\n", sub { 2; });

=== two bodies of one line keep their order
f(<<A, <<B,
first
A
second
B
  1);
--- facts
faithful
# f("first\n", "second\n", 1);

=== an indented heredoc in a list
my $x = 1; f(1,
<<~EOT, 2);
    a $x
    EOT
--- facts
faithful
# f(1, "a $x\n", 2);

=== an interpolating heredoc with a paren and a semicolon in its body
my $x = 1; f(<<"EOT",
a $x (;
EOT
  2);
--- facts
faithful

=== DESTROY without sub (op/hash.t, op/pos.t, op/vec.t)
{ package Class; DESTROY { ++$destroyed; } }
--- facts
faithful
# sub DESTROY { (++$destroyed); }

=== DESTROY without sub across lines (op/sub.t, op/undef.t)
DESTROY {
    $messages .= 'destroyed ';
}
--- facts
faithful

=== AUTOLOAD without sub
AUTOLOAD { 1; }
--- facts
faithful
# sub AUTOLOAD { 1; }

=== a body inside the statement, then one after it
f(<<A,
first
A
  <<B);
second
B
--- facts
faithful
# f("first\n", "second\n");
